steps.why: pure function of topics.txt: strip blanks, lowercase-dedupe, slugify. Runs must not differ. The shipped topics.txt already needs all three rules (7 lines, 1 blank, 1 case-variant dup, 1 exact dup, 4 unique slugs).

proposed_script.name: normalize_topics.py
proposed_script.stdout: counts: lines read, blanks dropped, duplicates dropped, unique slugs
proposed_script.exit: 0 at least one topic / 1 no usable topic / 2 usage

steps.why: WebFetch is a permission-gated agent tool, so the fetch itself cannot move into a script. The mechanical shell around it can: build the slug-to-path worklist, skip slugs already saved, and verify each saved file after the fetch.

proposed_script.name: fetch_plan.py
proposed_script.stdout: one 'slug<TAB>sources/<slug>.html<TAB>PENDING|CACHED' row per topic; with --verify, empty or non-HTML saves listed as FAILED
proposed_script.exit: 0 plan complete / 1 verify found empty or missing saves / 2 usage

steps.why: the user's keep/drop pick is the judgment and AskUserQuestion is an agent tool, but the option rows Claude presents are mechanical: one row per fetched source with word count, thin flag, and fetch status.

proposed_script.name: source_stats.py
proposed_script.stdout: per-source table: slug, words, THIN flag, and the AskUserQuestion option label for each
proposed_script.exit: 0 stats produced / 1 no sources found / 2 usage

steps.why: word count plus a fixed 200-word threshold. A unit test can be written against it today, and two runs counting the same file must agree.

proposed_script.name: source_stats.py
proposed_script.stdout: per-source table: slug, words, THIN flag
proposed_script.exit: 0 stats produced / 1 no sources found / 2 usage

steps.why: the notion MCP calls (page-id lookup, append) must stay Claude, because a script reimplementation loses auth and the permission model. The summary block appended to the page is a fixed template over stats.json, so the script renders the exact text Claude posts.

proposed_script.name: render_index.py
proposed_script.stdout: the rendered summary block (also written to --out)
proposed_script.exit: 0 rendered / 1 stats.json empty or malformed / 2 usage

steps.why: the 200-word brief in the house voice is the one output that should differ run to run; a script would encode one arbitrary summary. Its checkable bound (word count) is already covered by source_stats.py, so lint the drafts with that rather than scripting the writing.
sort stats.json by word count descending and emit a fixed three-column markdown table. No input varies the result.

proposed_script.name: render_index.py
proposed_script.stdout: the rendered index table (also written to --out)
proposed_script.exit: 0 rendered / 1 stats.json empty or malformed / 2 usage
